items.name: Zoom Camera Mast
items.description: Multispectral stereo cameras on a mast with zoom optics. Your eyes on Mars. Selecting it unlocks free camera control during the flight simulation.

items.name: Laser Spectrometer Mast
items.description: A rock-vaporizing laser with a telescope and spectrometers, mounted on the mast. Detects chemistry from metres away without driving to the target.

items.name: X-Ray Rock Analyzer
items.description: Precision X-ray fluorescence spectrometer that reads the elemental chemistry of rock grains up close. A Mars 2020 analyzer-class instrument.

items.name: UV Mineral Scanner
items.description: Ultraviolet spectrometer that detects organic compounds and minerals. Required by the Mars 2020 mission to hunt for signs of past microbial life.

items.name: Weather Station
items.description: Environmental sensors measuring temperature, pressure, wind and dust on the Martian surface. Light and affordable science.

items.name: Oxygen Generator Demo
items.description: Converts carbon dioxide into breathable oxygen. For automated missions it is a technology demo; for crewed missions it is critical life-support equipment. Leaving it off a crewed mission risks the lives of everyone on board.

items.name: Ground-Penetrating Radar
items.description: Radar that peers up to ten metres beneath the surface, revealing buried rock layers. The lightest instrument in the catalog.

items.name: Surface Science Station
items.description: Autonomous surface instruments (seismometer, magnetometer, heat flow) powered by a nuclear generator. The centerpiece of lunar surface science.

items.name: Sample Collection & Return Kit
items.description: Tools, containers and preservation systems for collecting lunar rock and soil and returning it to laboratories on Earth.

items.name: Crew EVA Science Kit
items.description: Hand-carried instruments and tools that astronauts use during surface walks to investigate sites no robotic arm can reach.
